title: The Sunday Read: ‘What Does It Mean to Save a Neighborhood?’

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日简报 Dealbook 的商业与政策记者。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域一些举足轻重的领袖，包括万斯

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的真实对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Kimmelman.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·金尔曼。

sentences.en: I'm the architecture critic for the Times and the founder and editor-at-large for Headway.
sentences.zh: 我是《时报》的建筑评论员，也是 Headway 的创始兼特约编辑。

sentences.en: Headway is a new initiative at the New York Times that I started, which is focused on global challenges and paths to progress.
sentences.zh: Headway 是我在《纽约时报》发起的一个新项目，专注于全球挑战和通往进步的途径。

sentences.en: It's intended, really, to try to promote a kind of constructive conversation around big issues to get away from some of the 24-hour news cycle
sentences.zh: 它的真正目的，是试图围绕重大议题推动一种建设性的对话，摆脱一些 24 小时滚动新闻周期的束缚

sentences.en: and focus, really, on how we, as a newspaper and we, more broadly, as a society, can think about these problems in the long term.
sentences.zh: 真正专注于作为一份报纸的我们，以及更广泛地作为社会的我们，如何能够长期思考这些问题。

sentences.en: We can promote a conversation that looks across time and not just about what's happening the next day.
sentences.zh: 我们可以推动一场跨越时间的对话，而不仅仅是关注第二天发生的事情。

sentences.en: The story is about a park in lower Manhattan called East River Park.
sentences.zh: 这个故事是关于曼哈顿下城一个叫做东河公园的公园。

sentences.en: I see the park as a kind of parable about democracy and how we make decisions today.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个公园就像是一个关于民主以及我们今天如何做出决策的寓言。

sentences.en: Very often, our system sort of grinds to a halt.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我们的系统有点陷入停滞。

sentences.en: And with challenges like climate change, where the scale and pace of them is so great,
sentences.zh: 面对气候变化这样规模和节奏都如此巨大的挑战，

sentences.en: I think the park is an example of the problem we face.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个公园就是我们所面临问题的一个例子。

sentences.en: How can we begin to think differently?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能开始有不同的思考？

sentences.en: And how can we examine some of these systems we have in place?
sentences.zh: 我们又如何能够审视我们现有的某些体制？

sentences.en: We have to begin by seeing how the system works or doesn't.
sentences.zh: 我们必须首先了解这个系统是如何运作的，或者说它是如何失效的。

sentences.en: And this is, I hope, what the park helps to show.
sentences.zh: 我希望，这正是这个公园所能展现的。

sentences.en: So East River Park was built in the 1930s by Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 所以东河公园是罗伯特·摩西在 20 世纪 30 年代建造的。

sentences.en: Much of New York City, as we now know it, was created by Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 正如我们现在所知，纽约市很大一部分都是由罗伯特·摩西创建的。

sentences.en: Not all of what Moses did was good.
sentences.zh: 摩西所做的事情并非全都是好事。

sentences.en: Much of it destroyed old neighborhoods, especially poor black and brown neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 其中大部分摧毁了旧社区，尤其是贫穷的黑人和棕色人种社区。

sentences.en: But one of the better things that he did was to build parks like East River Park that would benefit one of the poorest parts of the city.
sentences.zh: 但他做过的较好的事情之一，就是修建了像东河公园这样的公园，让这个城市最贫困的地区之一受益。

sentences.en: The park is essentially a ribbon, a kind of promenade that runs along the highway.
sentences.zh: 这个公园本质上是一条丝带，一种沿着高速公路延伸的长廊。

sentences.en: And on the other side of the highway are the housing projects.
sentences.zh: 而在高速公路的另一边则是经济适用房项目。

sentences.en: On a beautiful day or in the evening, it's just an astonishingly wonderful mix of New Yorkers from different communities who come together in that park.
sentences.zh: 在一个好天气里或傍晚，这里汇聚了来自不同社区的纽约人，形成了一种令人惊叹的美妙融合，他们在这个公园里聚在一起。

sentences.en: It's one of the most beautiful places in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 这是曼哈顿最美丽的地方之一。

sentences.en: In 2012, the park flooded with Hurricane Sandy and the public housing projects next to the park also flooded.
sentences.zh: 2012 年，飓风桑迪导致公园被淹，公园旁边的公共住房项目也未能幸免。

sentences.en: So the federal government came up with a plan to hold a competition that would come up with ideas to protect the park.
sentences.zh: 因此，联邦政府提出了一项计划，举办一场竞赛来征集保护公园的创意。

sentences.en: And at the heart of the competition was the idea that the community would participate in this process
sentences.zh: 而这场竞赛的核心思想是社区参与这一进程

sentences.en: and come up with a solution that would both work as flood protection and benefit the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 并提出一个既能起到防洪作用又能造福社区的解决方案。

sentences.en: And so what was supposed to be a sort of effort to combine infrastructure with community development
sentences.zh: 因此，原本应该是一项将基础设施与社区发展相结合的努力

sentences.en: has ended up dividing the community, and we haven't still had the first shovel put in the ground nine years later.
sentences.zh: 最终却导致了社区的分裂，九年过去了，我们甚至还没有动土开工。

sentences.en: So I grew up not so many blocks away from East River Park.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在距离东河公园不远的几个街区长大的。

sentences.en: Embedded in my lifeblood was a feeling that architecture, urbanism, was the story of who we are.
sentences.zh: 融入我血液中的是一种感觉，即建筑、城市主义，就是我们是谁的故事。

sentences.en: We are what we build.
sentences.zh: 我们建造了什么，我们就是什么。

sentences.en: So when I became an architecture critic, my interest was really in trying to make sure that the things that we wrote about
sentences.zh: 因此，当我成为一名建筑评论员时，我的兴趣其实在于确保我们所写的内容

sentences.en: respected architecture in all of its complexity, that it wasn't just about making things that looked like, you know, giant sculptures,
sentences.zh: 尊重建筑的复杂性，它不单单是建造看起来像巨型雕塑的东西，

sentences.en: but also making neighborhoods, making communities, what kind of a society we wanted to have.
sentences.zh: 而且还要建设街区、建设社区，以及我们想要拥有一个什么样的社会。

sentences.en: Because that really is, in a sense, the larger project of architecture for how we should think about building a society, building a larger world.
sentences.zh: 因为从某种意义上说，这确实是关于我们应该如何思考建设一个社会、建设一个更广阔世界的宏大建筑工程。

sentences.en: So here's my article.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我的文章。

sentences.en: What does it mean to save a neighborhood?
sentences.zh: 拯救一个社区意味着什么？

sentences.en: This story was written and narrated by Michael Kimmelman.
sentences.zh: 这个故事由迈克尔·金尔曼撰写并叙述。

sentences.en: download Autumn on the App Store or the Play Store.
sentences.zh: 请在 App Store 或 Play Store 下载 Autumn。

sentences.en: Visit autumn, that's A-U-D-M, dot com for details.
sentences.zh: 访问 autumn，即 A-U-D-M 点 com 了解详情。

sentences.en: The day after the storm swallowed her neighborhood, Nancy Ortiz woke before dawn to buy ice.
sentences.zh: 在风暴吞没她社区的第二天，南希·奥尔蒂斯在黎明前醒来去买冰块。

sentences.en: It was 2012, and Superstorm Sandy had reclaimed Lower Manhattan for Mother Nature.
sentences.zh: 那是 2012 年，超级风暴桑迪将曼哈顿下城重新带回给了大自然。

sentences.en: Making landfall near Atlantic City, it swept north, ravaging the New Jersey coast, destroying thousands of homes, and inundating New York City with waves as high as 14 feet.
sentences.zh: 它在大西洋城附近登陆，一路向北席卷，蹂躏了新泽西海岸，摧毁了数千栋房屋，并用高达 14 英尺的巨浪淹没了纽约市。

sentences.en: Sandy shuttered Wall Street, rattling global markets, and for a moment, the storm restored Manhattan's early 17th-century coastline.
sentences.zh: 桑迪让华尔街关门停业，震动了全球市场，一时间，这场风暴让曼哈顿恢复了 17 世纪初的海岸线。

sentences.en: A brackish murk of waist-high water submerged all the landfill that humans had dredged, salvaged, and shipped to widen the island, and that now supported the Franklin D.
sentences.zh: 齐腰深的微咸浑浊积水淹没人类为拓宽该岛而疏浚、打捞并运送的所有填海造陆，而这些土地现在支撑着富兰克林·D·

sentences.en: Roosevelt Drive.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福大道。

sentences.en: It also swamped a large cluster of public housing developments and a beloved but bedraggled ribbon of greenery built by Robert Moses during the 1930s called East River Park.
sentences.zh: 它还淹没了一大片公共住房开发区，以及由罗伯特·摩西在 20 世纪 30 年代建造的、备受喜爱却有些破败的绿化带——东河公园。

sentences.en: In the dark, Ms. Ortiz tiptoed through a shambles of overturned cars and shattered glass to her Acura TSX.
sentences.zh: 在黑暗中，奥尔蒂斯女士踩着满地的翻倒汽车和破碎玻璃，蹑手蹑脚地走向她的讴歌 TSX。

sentences.en: The storm had knocked out electricity to 250,000 people in the area, including those in Vladek houses, the oldest public housing project on the Lower East Side.
sentences.zh: 风暴切断了该地区 25 万人的电力供应，其中包括下东区最古老的公共住房项目瓦拉德克之家的居民。

sentences.en: As president of the Vladek Tenants Association, Ms. Ortiz knew there were many diabetic residents who would need to keep their insulin cold.
sentences.zh: 作为瓦拉德克租户协会的主席，奥尔蒂斯女士知道有许多患有糖尿病的居民需要冷藏他们的胰岛素。

sentences.en: She figured help wasn't likely to come quickly.
sentences.zh: 她觉得救援不会那么快到来。

sentences.en: For public housing residents, it rarely did.
sentences.zh: 对于公共住房居民来说，救援总是寥寥无几。

sentences.en: So she got into her car and headed north, some 15 miles, all the way into the Bronx, before finding a store selling 10-pound bags of ice.
sentences.zh: 于是她上车向北行驶了大约 15 英里，一路开到布朗克斯，才找到一家出售 10 磅装冰块的商店。

sentences.en: Into the night, she navigated Vladek's dark stairwells, knocking on doors.
sentences.zh: 夜色中，她摸索着穿过瓦拉德克黑暗的楼梯间，敲响了一扇扇门。

sentences.en: Though Ms. Ortiz's neighborhood was one of the worst hit by Sandy, the storm caused tens of billions of dollars in damage all across the region and killed more than 100 people.
sentences.zh: 尽管奥尔蒂斯女士的社区是受桑迪打击最严重的地区之一，但这场风暴在整个地区造成了数百亿美元的损失，并夺去了 100 多人的生命。

sentences.en: It was a sign of things to come and begged for a federal response.
sentences.zh: 这是未来灾难的一个预兆，并迫切需要联邦政府做出回应。

sentences.en: After surveying the wreckage, President Barack Obama turned to Sean Donovan, his director of housing and urban development,
sentences.zh: 在视察了残骸后，贝拉克·奥巴马总统找到了他的住房和城市发展部部长肖恩·多纳文，

sentences.en: who came up with a novel federal competition called Rebuild by Design.
sentences.zh: 他提出了一项名为“设计重建”的新颖联邦竞赛。

sentences.en: Teams of architects and engineers were invited to conceive creative flood protection proposals in collaboration with members of the affected communities.
sentences.zh: 建筑师和工程师团队应邀与受灾社区成员合作，构思富有创意的防洪方案。

sentences.en: Several dozen proposals surfaced, and in 2014, seven winners were selected.
sentences.zh: 几十个方案浮出水面，2014 年，七个优胜者脱颖而出。

sentences.en: By far, the largest grant went to a segment of a wider Lower Manhattan Resiliency Plan called the Big U.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，最大的一笔拨款授予了更广泛的曼哈顿下城韧性计划的一个部分，名为“大U”。

sentences.en: It aimed to protect residents in the public housing developments, including Vladek.
sentences.zh: 旨在保护公共住房开发区（包括瓦拉德克）的居民。

sentences.en: Officials named the segment the East Side Coastal Resiliency Project.
sentences.zh: 官员们将这一部分命名为“东侧海岸韧性项目”。

sentences.en: Borrowing ideas from the waterlogged Dutch, the plan imagined a redesigned East River Park that could withstand flooding from future Sandy-level events.
sentences.zh: 借鉴饱受水患的荷兰人的想法，该计划设想对东河公园进行重新设计，使其能够抵御未来桑迪级别事件带来的洪水。

sentences.en: A grassy-reinforced hill, or berm, on the western edge of the park abutting the FDR Drive, would be built to act as a barrier,
sentences.zh: 将在紧邻 FDR 大道的公园西缘建造一座草皮加固的小山（或路堤），作为屏障，

sentences.en: holding back floodwaters and protecting the housing developments.
sentences.zh: 阻挡洪水并保护住房开发区。

sentences.en: The plan went through years of public workshops, town hall meetings, and open houses, attended by more than 1,000 community members.
sentences.zh: 该计划经历了多年的公众研讨会、市政厅会议和开放日活动，有 1000 多名社区成员参加。

sentences.en: Its estimated price tag was $760 million.
sentences.zh: 其估计造价为 7.6 亿美元。

sentences.en: New York City taxpayers would pay for what the federal government's grant didn't cover.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府拨款未涵盖的部分将由纽约市纳税人支付。

sentences.en: I had followed Rebuild from the start, as an architecture critic focused on public space, housing, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 作为一名专注于公共空间、住房和环境的建筑评论员，我从一开始就关注着重建计划。

sentences.en: I saw the effort as a genuine breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 我认为这项努力是一个真正的突破。

sentences.en: The political stars looked as if they might align federal, state, and city governments, as well as neighborhood groups,
sentences.zh: 政治上的各种力量似乎有望联合起来——联邦、州和市政府以及社区群体，

sentences.en: all pulling in unison to tackle climate change on a meaningful scale in ways that prioritize design and the needs of vulnerable populations.
sentences.zh: 大家齐心协力，以有意义的规模应对气候变化，同时优先考虑设计和弱势群体的需求。

sentences.en: Rebuild, in spirit at least, harked back to the creative, can-do days of the New Deal and the space program.
sentences.zh: “重建”计划至少在精神上让人回想起新政和太空计划时期那种充满创意、志在必得的日子。

sentences.en: I visited sites with Mr. Donovan, sat in on meetings, and invited the plans architects to graduate classes I taught on climate change in global cities at Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 我与多纳文先生一起实地考察，参加会议，并邀请该计划的建筑师到我在哥伦比亚大学教授的关于全球城市气候变化的研究生班上课。

sentences.en: The architects told the students about the slow, incremental process of earning neighborhood support.
sentences.zh: 建筑师们向学生们讲述了争取社区支持的缓慢、渐进的过程。

sentences.en: They came with glossy renderings of Photoshop joggers and parents-pushing strollers in the reimagined park, where floods came and went.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了光鲜亮丽的渲染图，上面有使用 Photoshop 添加的慢跑者，以及在洪水来来去去的改造后公园里推着婴儿车的父母。

sentences.en: But then, in 2018, under Mayor Bill de Blasio, the mood changed.
sentences.zh: 但随后在 2018 年，在市长白思豪的领导下，气氛发生了变化。

sentences.en: Behind closed doors, city agencies did a constructability review.
sentences.zh: 在闭门会议中，市政府机构进行了施工可行性审查。

sentences.en: That is, they calculated the proposal's costs and timeline, and concluded that it was simply not feasible.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们计算了该提案的成本和时间表，并得出结论认为这根本不可行。

sentences.en: The city's parks department said it didn't have the money, workers, or expertise to maintain infrastructure in a park built to flood.
sentences.zh: 纽约市公园部门表示，它没有资金、人手或专业知识来维护一个专为蓄洪而建的公园中的基础设施。

sentences.en: The Department of Transportation, prioritizing cars and trucks, decided the berm's construction would be too disruptive to traffic on the FDR drive.
sentences.zh: 交通运输部将轿车和卡车放在首位，认为路堤的建设对 FDR 大道的交通干扰太大。

sentences.en: Con Edison said that the proposal would interfere with its underground power lines,
sentences.zh: 联合爱迪生公司表示，该提案将干扰其地下电力线，

sentences.en: and that engineering the necessary tunnels to encase the lines could add years, risks, and untold costs to the project.
sentences.zh: 并且为电线修建必要管道的工程将给项目增加多年的工期、风险和无法估量的成本。

sentences.en: City Hall unveiled what it called an alternative design.
sentences.zh: 市政府公布了他们所谓的替代设计。

sentences.en: It would cost New Yorkers $1.45 billion.
sentences.zh: 这将花费纽约人 14.5 亿美元。

sentences.en: It required raising not a portion of the park, like the earlier plan, but the entire park,
sentences.zh: 它不再像之前的计划那样只抬高公园的一部分，而是要求抬高整个公园，

sentences.en: and then covering nearly all its 50-odd acres with 8 to 10 feet of landfill, while keeping Con Ed's power lines accessible.
sentences.zh: 然后用 8 到 10 英尺的填土覆盖其近 50 英亩的土地，同时保持联合爱迪生公司的电力线可触及。

sentences.en: A new East River Park, much like the one envisioned by the architects and community groups, would be built on top of the landfill with new areas for passive recreation.
sentences.zh: 一个新的东河公园将在填土之上建造，很像建筑师和社区团体设想的那样，并设有用于消极休闲的新区域。

sentences.en: Gone was the idea of periodic, acceptable flooding.
sentences.zh: 定期且可接受的洪水的想法不复存在了。

sentences.en: The new raised park, braced by a 1.2-mile flood wall and millions of tons of layered earth barged in by water, would act as a levee to hold back the surging sea.
sentences.zh: 这座崭新且抬高的公园由一条 1.2 英里长的防洪墙和通过水路运来的数百万吨分层土壤支撑，将起到堤坝的作用，挡住汹涌的海水。

sentences.en: When the mayor announced the plan, I started to hear new voices.
sentences.zh: 当市长宣布该计划时，我开始听到不同的声音。

sentences.en: A group, led by professors, artists, and other lower Manhattan residents, a number of whom didn't live next to the park but used it, started organizing protests.
sentences.zh: 一个由教授、艺术家和其他曼哈顿下城居民（其中许多人不住在公园旁边但经常使用它）领导的群体开始组织抗议活动。

sentences.en: They argued that the city's new plan did not go far enough to address the effects of climate change, and that demolishing the park with the shade of a thousand mature trees
sentences.zh: 他们认为，市政府的新计划在应对气候变化的影响方面还不够彻底，拆除拥有上千棵成熟大树树荫的公园，

sentences.en: would leave the neighborhood without precious green space for years.
sentences.zh: 将使该社区在多年里失去宝贵的绿地。

sentences.en: They contested the city's experts, who said the park couldn't be maintained as a gigantic sponge.
sentences.zh: 他们反驳了市政府专家的说法，即该公园无法作为一块巨大的海绵来维护。

sentences.en: I saw pictures of them chaining themselves to trees and noticed they enlisted a lawyer who had opposed other city initiatives, including rapid bus lanes on 14th Street.
sentences.zh: 我看到他们把自己锁在树上的照片，并注意到他们请了一位曾反对过其他城市倡议的律师，其中包括 14 号大街的快速公交车道。

sentences.en: Ms. Ortiz and some of her neighbors in the subsidized housing projects were no less appalled by the mayor's sudden change of plans.
sentences.zh: 奥尔蒂斯女士和她在经济适用房项目中的一些邻居对市长突然改变计划同样感到震惊。

sentences.en: We felt betrayed, like we didn't exist, was how Ms. Ortiz put it to me.
sentences.zh: 奥尔蒂斯女士对我说：“我们感到被背叛了，就像我们根本不存在一样。”

sentences.en: But they also wanted something, anything, built as soon as possible to protect them from the flooding of future Sandys.
sentences.zh: 但他们也希望尽快建造一些东西——任何东西——来保护他们免受未来桑迪式洪水的侵袭。

sentences.en: They started to accept the merits of the city's plan.
sentences.zh: 他们开始接受市政府计划的优点。

sentences.en: As they did so, they began to see its opponents as interlopers, more than a few of them wealthier white people living in apartments that were not on the front lines.
sentences.zh: 随着他们这样做，他们开始将反对者视为闯入者，其中不乏住在并不处于前线公寓里的较富裕的白人。

sentences.en: A project devised to build community trust and overcome political gridlock seemed to be fracturing the community instead.
sentences.zh: 一个旨在建立社区信任并克服政治僵局的项目，结果似乎反而使社区分裂了。

sentences.en: Now, nearly a decade after Sandy, the Lower East Side is still vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 现在，在桑迪过去近十年后，下东区仍然十分脆弱。

sentences.en: Across the country, there are similar daunting challenges that demand big, robust, and swift responses.
sentences.zh: 在全国各地，都有类似严峻的挑战，需要做出宏大、有力且迅速的响应。

sentences.en: There's climate change, of course, which brings extreme weather and rising seas, but also a dearth of affordable housing, an electric grid in disrepair,
sentences.zh: 当然有气候变化，它带来了极端天气和海平面上升，还有经济适用房的短缺、失修的电网、

sentences.en: a lack of broadband access, failing public transit systems, the list goes on and on.
sentences.zh: 缺乏宽带接入、公共交通系统失效，这样的例子不胜枚举。

sentences.en: The recent passage of a $1.2 trillion federal infrastructure bill is a big step toward tackling some of those probleMs.
sentences.zh: 最近通过的 1.2 万亿美元联邦基础设施法案是解决其中一些问题的重要一步。

sentences.en: But, as East River Park shows, even when money is at hand, our convoluted systems often make it difficult or impossible to find consensus and work at the speed and scale required.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如东河公园所展示的那样，即使资金到位，我们错综复杂的体制往往也让人难以或无法达成共识，并以所需的急迫速度和规模推进工作。

sentences.en: A process of participatory planning, rightly evolved to represent interests other than government
sentences.zh: 参与式规划的过程，本是为了代表政府技术官僚和富有开发商以外的利益而正确演变而来的，

sentences.en: technocrats and wealthy developers, has also created, in some places, a culture of nimbyism that thwarts even modest proposals.
sentences.zh: 但在某些地方，也产生了一种“邻避”文化，甚至阻挠了温和的提案。

sentences.en: Our conversations seem increasingly cramped, mean, and small.
sentences.zh: 我们的对话似乎越来越局促、刻薄和狭隘。

sentences.en: Is our society just too frayed to come together around basic material needs?
sentences.zh: 我们的社会是不是已经太四分五裂，以至于无法围绕基本物质需求凝聚在一起？

sentences.en: In the debate over what is officially called John V.
sentences.zh: 在关于官方称之为约翰·V·

sentences.en: Lindsay, East River Park,
sentences.zh: 林赛东河公园的辩论中，

sentences.en: I sensed there might be some useful lessons about how we got here and how we might try to think differently.
sentences.zh: 我感觉到，关于我们是如何走到这一步的以及我们如何才能进行不同的思考，可能会有一些有用的教训。

sentences.en: The park saga is not a conflict between bad versus good actors, but a confluence of different interests, different areas of expertise, different notions of community.
sentences.zh: 这场公园传奇并不是好人与坏人之间的冲突，而是不同利益、不同专业领域、不同社区观念的交汇。

sentences.en: It is a parable of progress.
sentences.zh: 这是关于进步的一个寓言。

sentences.en: Construction on enormous flood walls north of the park has begun.
sentences.zh: 公园北部巨型防洪墙的建设已经开始。

sentences.en: The city had planned to start reconstruction in the park itself by late November, until a judge granted opponents a temporary stay.
sentences.zh: 市政府原计划在 11 月下旬开始公园本身的重建，直到一名法官批准了反对者的临时暂缓令。

sentences.en: The stay has just been lifted, and park construction is supposed to take five years.
sentences.zh: 该暂缓令刚刚被解除，公园建设预计需要五年时间。

sentences.en: If completed, the new park certainly won't be the best thing that we could achieve.
sentences.zh: 如果建成，这个新公园肯定不会是我们能取得的最佳成果。

sentences.en: Far from it.
sentences.zh: 远非如此。

sentences.en: And it may need to be rebuilt to cope with even more extreme weather in the future.
sentences.zh: 为了应对未来更极端的天气，它可能需要重新修建。

sentences.en: But nor is it a certain calamity.
sentences.zh: 但它也并非注定是一场灾难。

sentences.en: It's a hefty public investment to benefit thousands of underserved New Yorkers that should provide some protection from flooding for a time.
sentences.zh: 这是一项沉重的公共投资，旨在造福成千上万服务不足的纽约人，应该能在一段时间内提供一定的防洪保护。

sentences.en: An incremental step, in other words.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这是一个渐进的步骤。

sentences.en: Incrementalism is how we think about progress today.
sentences.zh: 渐进主义就是我们今天对进步的看法。

sentences.en: The question is, are there other ways to think about it?
sentences.zh: 问题是，还有没有其他思考方式？

sentences.en: In 1939, George Gallup's American Institute of Public Opinion conducted a national poll.
sentences.zh: 1939 年，乔治·盖洛普的美国民意研究所进行了一项全国民意调查。

sentences.en: With the country coming out of the Depression, pollsters asked Americans to name both the Roosevelt administration's greatest accomplishment and lowest point.
sentences.zh: 随着国家走出大萧条，民意调查人员要求美国人说出罗斯福政府最大的成就和最低谷。

sentences.en: The New Deal had by then established Social Security and Federal Bank Deposit Insurance.
sentences.zh: 当时，新政已经建立了社会保障和联邦存款保险。

sentences.en: But what became known as the Work Projects Administration was arguably its most ambitious program.
sentences.zh: 但后来被称为“公共事业振兴署”的项目可以说是其最具雄心的计划。

sentences.en: A vast menu of public works, coordinated with local and state authorities, the WPA employed millions of Americans.
sentences.zh: 作为与地方和州当局协调的庞大公共工程菜单，WPA 雇用了数百万美国人。

sentences.en: Across the nation, it produced new schools, hospitals, sewers, and hydroelectric power plants, as well as murals, sculptures, libraries, LaGuardia Airport in Queens,
sentences.zh: 在全国范围内，它修建了新的学校、医院、下水道和水力发电厂，还有壁画、雕塑、图书馆、皇后区的拉瓜迪亚机场，

sentences.en: and some 650,000 miles of roads and 8,000 parks.
sentences.zh: 以及大约 65 万英里的道路和 8000 个公园。

sentences.en: It transformed America.
sentences.zh: 它改变了美国。

sentences.en: As the historian Jason Scott Smith tells it, In the Gallup survey, the WPA was ranked as both the best and worst thing the administration had done.
sentences.zh: 正如历史学家杰森·斯科特·史密斯所说，在盖洛普的调查中，WPA 被评为该届政府做过的最好和最坏的事情。

sentences.en: Change, big change especially, always profits some and troubles others.
sentences.zh: 变革，尤其是巨大的变革，总是让一部分人受益，让另一部分人烦恼。

sentences.en: Among the roads funded by the WPA was a section of the FDR Drive, then called East River Drive.
sentences.zh: 在由WPA（工程进展署）资助的道路中，有一段是FDR大道，当时被称为东河大道。

sentences.en: To city leaders nearly a century ago, New York's economic future hinged on suburban commuters and automobiles.
sentences.zh: 在将近一个世纪前的城市领导人看来，纽约的经济未来取决于郊区通勤者和汽车。

sentences.en: Car dependence now seems spectacularly wrong-headed to urban planners, ecologists, and transit advocates,
sentences.zh: 在城市规划者、生态学家和交通倡导者看来，对汽车的依赖现在显得错得离谱，

sentences.en: with all we know about sprawl, carbon emissions, and the way highways divided and segregated city neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 考虑到我们对城市扩张、碳排放以及公路如何分割和隔离城市街区的所有了解。

sentences.en: But what is regarded as progress at one moment often comes to be seen as the problem later.
sentences.zh: 但一个时期被认为是进步的事物，往往在后来会被视为问题。

sentences.en: As Eric Kleinenberg, a sociology professor at New York University, puts it,
sentences.zh: 正如纽约大学社会学教授埃里克·克莱嫩伯格所说，

sentences.en: Science is based on the premise that we will inevitably be wrong and find better ways to make sense of things.
sentences.zh: 科学的前提是，我们不可避免地会犯错，并找到更好的方法来理解事物。

sentences.en: Social reformers in the 1930s seized on the highway's construction to lobby for the creation of new forms of public housing next to the new East River Drive.
sentences.zh: 20世纪30年代的社会改革者抓住公路建设的机会，游说在新的东河大道旁兴建新型公共住房。

sentences.en: Vladek Houses, the first of these developments, opened in 1940, a complex of twenty six-story brick apartment blocks featuring modern conveniences like
sentences.zh: 弗拉德克公寓（Vladek Houses）是这些开发项目中的第一个，于1940年开放，这是一个由26层砖砌公寓楼组成的综合体，配备了诸如

sentences.en: self-operating elevators, as one news report noted.
sentences.zh: 自动运行电梯等现代便利设施，正如一条新闻报道所指出的那样。

sentences.en: In contrast to the cramped airless tenements that made the turn-of-the-century Lower East Side notorious for overcrowding and outbreaks of cholera and other diseases,
sentences.zh: 与世纪之交下东区因过度拥挤以及霍乱和其他疾病暴发而臭名昭著的狭窄、不通风的筒子楼相比，

sentences.en: Vladek's boxy buildings in wide-open spaces represented progressive ideals about humane living and public health.
sentences.zh: 弗拉德克方正的建筑和开阔的空间代表了关于人道居住和公共健康的进步理想。

sentences.en: More than 19,000 New Yorkers applied for 1,771 subsidized departments before officials had to put a halt to applications.
sentences.zh: 超过19,000名纽约市民申请1,771套补贴公寓，之后官员们不得不叫停申请。

sentences.en: Robert Moses, then New York's Parks Commissioner, saw another opportunity in the highway's construction.
sentences.zh: 时任纽约市公园专员的罗伯特·摩西在公路建设中看到了另一个机会。

sentences.en: The East River, down to the Battery, had once formed the heart of one of the mightiest and most prosperous ports in the world.
sentences.zh: 一直延伸到巴特利的东河，曾经是世界上最强大、最繁荣的港口之一的核心。

sentences.en: By the 1930s, however, maritime traffic had shifted across town to the deeper channels of the Hudson River.
sentences.zh: 然而，到了20世纪30年代，海上交通已经转移到城另一侧哈德逊河更深的水道上。

sentences.en: In 1937, Moses persuaded city officials to add acres of landfill along the East River waterfront,
sentences.zh: 1937年，摩西说服市官员沿东河滨水区添加数英亩的填海造地，

sentences.en: expanding Manhattan's shoreline, and creating a slender, gracious park with wading pools, baseball fields, shuffleboard courts, an open-air dance floor,
sentences.zh: 扩大了曼哈顿的海岸线，并建造了一个狭长而优雅的公园，内设戏水池、棒球场、沙壶球场、露天舞池，

sentences.en: and an amphitheater where, among other things, Shakespeare in the park would make its debut.
sentences.zh: 还有一个露天剧场，其中包括“公园里的莎士比亚”将在那里上演首秀。

sentences.en: Shaded by London plains and pin oak trees, the park was sandwiched between the new highway and a riverside promenade.
sentences.zh: 公园里绿树成荫，种植着伦敦悬铃木和湿地松，夹在新公路和河滨长廊之间。

sentences.en: One of Moses' less-heralded triumphs, East River Park opened in 1939.
sentences.zh: 东河公园于1939年开放，这是摩西鲜受赞誉的成就之一。

sentences.en: Three years later, Nancy Ortiz's recently widowed grandmother left Puerto Rico and settled into a tenement on Delancey Street
sentences.zh: 三年后，南希·奥蒂斯的祖母新丧丈夫，带着七个孩子离开波多黎各，在德兰西街的一栋筒子楼里安顿下来，

sentences.en: in the heart of the Lower East Side with her seven children.
sentences.zh: 这里位于下东区的中心地带。

sentences.en: The youngest, Nancy's future father, was 12-year-old Diego, who was called Willie, though no one can recall why.
sentences.zh: 最小的孩子是南希未来的父亲、12岁的迭戈，大家都叫他威利，尽管没人记得为什么。

sentences.en: East River Park, a couple of blocks away, became Willie's backyard.
sentences.zh: 几个街区之外的东河公园成了威利的后花园。

sentences.en: Years later, after returning from the Korean War, Willie moved a little closer to the park, into a development called Lavenberg Homes.
sentences.zh: 多年后，从朝鲜战争归来，威利搬到了离公园更近一点的地方，住进了一个名为拉芬伯格住宅（Lavenberg Homes）的开发项目。

sentences.en: Nancy grew up there.
sentences.zh: 南希就是在那里长大的。

sentences.en: As a little girl, Ms. Ortiz recalls, she would accompany her father to the park on summer weekends.
sentences.zh: 奥蒂斯女士回忆说，作为小女孩，她会在夏天的周末陪父亲去公园。

sentences.en: Willie and other men from the neighborhood would play softball in guayaberas and dress shoes, while she played tag with her friends.
sentences.zh: 威利和邻里里的其他男人穿着盖尤巴拉衬衫和正装皮鞋打垒球，而她则和朋友们玩捉迷藏。

sentences.en: Kids who skipped school, she remembers, would hide from truant officers behind the amphitheater.
sentences.zh: 她记得，逃学的孩子们会躲在露天剧场后面躲避旷课官员。

sentences.en: For Moses, the 1940s and 50s were years of peak authority as the city's planning czar.
sentences.zh: 对摩西来说，20世纪40和50年代作为城市规划沙皇是其权力的巅峰时期。

sentences.en: Among other things, he oversaw the addition of more public housing developments along the East River.
sentences.zh: 除其他事项外，他监督了沿东河增建更多公共住房项目的工作。

sentences.en: But the 1960s brought new thinking.
sentences.zh: 但20世纪60年代带来了新的思潮。

sentences.en: Rachel Carson, the marine biologist and author, challenged the authority of pesticide-making chemical companies and inspired the environmental movement.
sentences.zh: 海洋生物学家兼作家雷切尔·卡逊挑战了制造杀虫剂的化工公司的权威，并启发了环保运动。

sentences.en: Jane Jacobs took on the urban planning establishment.
sentences.zh: 简·雅各布斯向城市规划体制发起挑战。

sentences.en: The highways Moses built had demolished and physically split neighborhoods, displacing or isolating thousands of black and brown residents and fouling the air with car exhauSt.
sentences.zh: 摩西修建的高速公路拆毁并从物理上分割了街区，导致数千名黑人和棕色人种居民流离失所或被孤立，并用汽车尾气污染了空气。

sentences.en: Jacobs argued that ordinary residents who saw the city from the sidewalk level, not planners like Moses looking down on maps like demigods or developers focused on profits,
sentences.zh: 雅各布斯认为，从人行道高度看待城市的普通居民，而不是像半神一样俯视地图的摩西这样的规划者，或是专注于利润的开发商，

sentences.en: knew best what ought to be saved or built in their own neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 才最清楚他们自己的街区应该保留或建设什么。

sentences.en: Community members were the true experts.
sentences.zh: 社区成员才是真正的专家。

sentences.en: Moses' power waned.
sentences.zh: 摩西的权力开始减弱。

sentences.en: By the early 1970s, when Ms. Ortiz and her parents moved from Lavenberg into one of the newer Moses developments on Delancey Street,
sentences.zh: 到20世纪70年代初，当奥蒂斯女士和她的父母从拉芬伯格搬到德兰西街摩西更新的开发项目之一时，

sentences.en: an idea called Westway started to take shape across town.
sentences.zh: 一个名为“西线”（Westway）的想法开始在城另一侧成形。

sentences.en: The Westside Piers, which had replaced those on the East River, had by then become obsolete too, and Westway was a plan to reimagine that waterfront.
sentences.zh: 取代了东河码头的西区码头到那时也已过时，“西线”是一项重新构想该滨水区的计划。

sentences.en: A new interstate would be tunneled below the Hudson River, removing cars and trucks from city streets.
sentences.zh: 一条新的州际公路将被开凿在哈德逊河下方，从而将汽车和卡车从城市街道上移走。

sentences.en: Disused warehouses and docks would make way for apartments and commercial development.
sentences.zh: 废弃的仓库和码头将为公寓和商业开发让路。

sentences.en: As with East River Park, acres of landfill would be added to create a vast green esplanade.
sentences.zh: 与东河公园一样，将通过填海造地来创造一片广阔的绿色滨海大道。

sentences.en: Over the next decade and a half, Westway secured endorsements from New York's governors and mayors, and President Ronald Reagan's administration agreed to pay to move the highway.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的十五年里，“西线”获得了纽约州长和市长的支持，罗纳德·里根总统的政府同意出资搬迁这条高速公路。

sentences.en: But it wasn't to be.
sentences.zh: 但事与愿违。

sentences.en: The culture had shifted.
sentences.zh: 文化已经发生了转变。

sentences.en: As more Black and Hispanic tenants moved into public housing, federal and local authorities lost interest in its upkeep.
sentences.zh: 随着越来越多的黑人和西班牙裔租户搬进公房，联邦和地方当局对公房维护失去了兴趣。

sentences.en: Developments like Vladek, once advertised as bucolic and equitable alternatives to dense city living, came to represent urban decline.
sentences.zh: 像弗拉德克这样的开发项目，曾被宣传为高密度城市生活的田园诗般且公平的替代方案，如今却代表了城市的衰落。

sentences.en: With Westway, newly energized urban activists seized on the proposal as an outmoded emblem of Moses-style, top-down arrogance, though it wasn't Moses' idea.
sentences.zh: 在“西线”项目上，新焕发活力的城市活动人士将这一提案当作摩西式自上而下傲慢的过时象征，尽管这并不是摩西的主意。

sentences.en: They said it prioritized drivers, not public transit users, developers, not blue-collar New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 他们说，该项目优先考虑的是司机而非公共交通乘客，是开发商而非蓝领纽约人。

sentences.en: Environmentalists focused on its potential to disrupt the mating patterns of striped bass in the Hudson River.
sentences.zh: 环保主义者则关注它破坏哈德逊河条纹鲈鱼交配模式的潜在影响。

sentences.en: A coalition of wildlife advocates, architectural preservationists, and subway riders capitalizing on new Nixon-era ecological regulations challenged government experts in court.
sentences.zh: 野生动物倡导者、建筑保护主义者和地铁乘客组成的联盟，利用尼克松时代的新生态法规，在法庭上向政府专家发起了挑战。

sentences.en: And they won.
sentences.zh: 他们赢了。

sentences.en: Whether, in retrospect, Westway's defeat was a victory for the city or not,
sentences.zh: 不管事后看来“西线”的失败对这座城市而言是否算是一场胜利，

sentences.en: in effect, environmentalists derailed what would have been a greenway roughly twice the size of East River Park.
sentences.zh: 实际上，环保主义者破坏了一个面积大约是东河公园两倍的绿道计划。

sentences.en: It was definitely a triumph for grassroots organizers, signaling a new era in participatory democracy.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是基层组织者的胜利，标志着参与式民主的新时代。

sentences.en: The powers that be had begun to yield, however reluctantly and performatively, to people power.
sentences.zh: 当权者开始向民众力量妥协，尽管心不甘情愿且流于形式。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在App内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall, to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你尚未订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》App，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: When Rebuild for Design endorsed the Eastside Coastal Resiliency Project, the big idea was that it would be radically inclusive.
sentences.zh: 当“设计重建”组织支持东区海岸韧性项目时，其核心理念是实现极具包容性的参与。

sentences.en: The flood-proofing of East River Park would do more than protect the neighborhood from storm surges, its organizers said.
sentences.zh: 组织者表示，东河公园的防洪工程不仅能保护社区免受风暴潮侵袭，

sentences.en: It would marry elite architecture and urban planning with meaningful public engagement.
sentences.zh: 它还将把精英建筑与城市规划同有意义的公众参与结合起来。

sentences.en: People power would join up with expertise.
sentences.zh: 民众力量将与专业知识相结合。

sentences.en: In 2013, Lower Eastsiders began to meet with representatives from One Architecture and Urbanism
sentences.zh: 2013年，下东区居民开始与“一个建筑与城市主义”（One Architecture and Urbanism）的代表会面，

sentences.en: and the Bjorka Ingels Group, better known as BIG, the high-profile Danish architecture firm.
sentences.zh: 以及知名丹麦建筑事务所“比亚克·英格斯集团”（简称BIG）。

sentences.en: This group had come up with the multi-part plan, called the Big U, for protecting all of Lower Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 这个团队提出了名为“大U”（Big U）的多部分计划，旨在保护整个下曼哈顿。

sentences.en: Jeremy Siegel, one of BIG's architects, remembers lugging models and maps to community centers and public schools to show residents what the park could look like.
sentences.zh: 杰里米·西格尔是BIG的一名建筑师，他记得曾把模型和地图搬到社区中心和公立学校，向居民展示公园可能的样子。

sentences.en: He enjoyed the back-and-forth, he told me, and described the rounds of meetings as, quote, a slow, iterative process.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他很享受这种互动，并形容几轮会议是一个“缓慢的、迭代的过程”。

sentences.en: Matthijs Bau, the Dutch founder of One Architecture and a co-leader of the BIG team,
sentences.zh: 马蒂斯·鲍是“一个建筑”的荷兰创始人和BIG团队的共同负责人，

sentences.en: recalls that community members at first expressed fear about displacement, along with a good dose of distruSt.
sentences.zh: 他回忆说，社区成员最初对流离失所表达了担忧，同时还抱有相当程度的不信任。

sentences.en: For him, a key moment was when a local organizer, who had been skeptical of the plan, stood up and said that, quote, this was the first time residents were treated like partners.
sentences.zh: 对他而言，一个关键时刻是一位当地组织者站出来说，这“是居民第一次被当作合作伙伴对待”，而这位组织者之前曾对该计划持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Ms. Ortiz, who became a co-chair of a community board task force, recalls seniors lobbying for benches and tables where they could play cards,
sentences.zh: 奥蒂斯女士后来成为了社区董事会工作组的联合主席，她回忆说，老年人游说增加长椅和桌子供他们打牌，

sentences.en: and families petitioning for outdoor movie screenings.
sentences.zh: 而家庭则请愿增加户外电影放映。

sentences.en: People from the neighborhood wanted to see themselves in the process, she told me.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，来自社区的人们希望在这个过程中看到自己的身影。

sentences.en: Over time, we felt we were being heard.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，我们觉得自己的声音被听到了。

sentences.en: That is the goal of participatory decision-making, after all, to borrow a phrase from Malcolm Arouse, a graduate student at New York University,
sentences.zh: 借用纽约大学研究生马尔科姆·阿鲁斯的一句话，这毕竟就是参与式决策的目标，

sentences.en: who was writing his dissertation about the park, public trust requires participants to, quote,
sentences.zh: 他当时正在撰写关于该公园的学位论文，他指出公众信任要求参与者，引述如下：

sentences.en: continuously recognize their inputs reflected in the evolution, close quote, of a project.
sentences.zh: “持续认识到他们的意见反映在项目的演变中。”引述完毕。

sentences.en: So, when Mayor Bill de Blasio's administration, which had not raised insuperable objections during nearly five years of community consultation,
sentences.zh: 因此，当比尔·德布拉西奥市长的政府在近五年的社区协商期间没有提出不可逾越的反对意见时，

sentences.en: suddenly swapped the plan for what officials decided was a more technically sound one, the switch did more than infuriate residents.
sentences.zh: 却突然将计划替换为官员们认为技术上更合理的方案，这一转变不仅仅是激怒了居民。

sentences.en: It caused the legitimacy crisis.
sentences.zh: 它引发了一场合法性危机。

sentences.en: Residents felt bamboozled.
sentences.zh: 居民们感觉受到了愚弄。

sentences.en: The whole consulting process suddenly seemed like a sham.
sentences.zh: 整个协商过程突然看起来像是一场骗局。

sentences.en: And if that were the case, opponents asked, why should anyone believe city officials who said the engineering, construction, and maintenance costs made the earlier plan impossible?
sentences.zh: 反对者质问，如果真是这样，为什么大家还要相信那些宣称工程、建设和维护成本导致前期计划无法实现的市政府官员？

sentences.en: Well, expertise itself was now up for debate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，专业知识本身现在也受到了性质上的质疑。

sentences.en: We understand the frustration, said Jamie Torres-Springer, who was first deputy commissioner of the city's Department of Design and Construction, when the new plan was announced.
sentences.zh: 新计划公布时，市设计建设局第一副局长杰米·托雷斯-斯普林格表示：“我们理解这种挫败感。”

sentences.en: In retrospect, he told me, it would have been better to explain more clearly the city's perspective to residents in community meetings before announcing it as a done deal.
sentences.zh: 他告诉记者，在将其宣布为既定事实之前，在社区会议上更清晰地向居民解释市府的视角会更好。

sentences.en: But, quote, We were facing a deadline to spend the federal funds and wanted to get the project built as quickly as possible to get the flood protection in place, he added.
sentences.zh: 但他补充说：“我们面临着花光联邦资金的期限，并希望尽快建成该项目以落实防洪保护。”

sentences.en: We really didn't consider the new design to be a radical change from the original one.
sentences.zh: “我们真的不认为新设计与原设计有根本性的改变。”

sentences.en: Except, of course, that a central goal of the whole process, to build trust, had been undermined.
sentences.zh: 当然，除了整个过程的一个核心目标——建立信任——已经被破坏了这一事实之外。

sentences.en: I met recently with a half-dozen members of East River Park Action, the most vociferous of the opposition groups that arose in response to the new plan.
sentences.zh: 我最近会见了半打“东河公园行动”（East River Park Action）的成员，这是针对新计划而涌现的最激进的反对派组织。

sentences.en: Months earlier, the group's alerts started dropping in my inbox, announcing a court hearing or inviting people to join a protest march.
sentences.zh: 几个月前，该组织的提醒邮件开始塞满我的收箱，通报法庭听证会或邀请人们参加抗议游行。

sentences.en: We gathered around a table at Café Mogador, an old Middle Eastern standby in the East Village.
sentences.zh: 我们在东村的一家老牌中东餐馆摩加多尔咖啡馆（Café Mogador）的一张桌子周围聚在一起。

sentences.en: The group included Pat Arnau, a photographer,
sentences.zh: 该小组成员包括摄影师帕特·阿瑙、

sentences.en: Billy Cohen, a landscape designer, and Eileen Miles, a poet and the author of Chelsea Girls.
sentences.zh: 景观设计师比利·科恩，以及诗人兼《切尔西女孩》作者艾琳·迈尔斯。

sentences.en: Their distrust of the mayor's plan has been exacerbated by the city's refusal to turn over documents about its constructability study.
sentences.zh: 由于市政府拒绝交出关于其可施工性研究的文件，他们对市长计划的不信任感进一步加剧。

sentences.en: We had to do a Freedom of Information Law request, and the city finally released a heavily redacted version of the study, Ms. Arnau said.
sentences.zh: 阿瑙女士说：“我们不得不提出《信息自由法》申请，市府最终发布了一份经过大量涂黑的研究报告。”

sentences.en: Why should we believe anything the city says if it keeps hiding the truth?
sentences.zh: “如果市府不断隐瞒真相，我们凭什么相信它说的任何话？”

sentences.en: Ms. Arnau's group supported the original Berm idea that had been developed with the community and imagined the East River waterfront gradually transforming into wetlands.
sentences.zh: 阿瑙女士的组织支持最初与社区共同制定的护堤构想，并设想东河滨水区逐渐转变为湿地。

sentences.en: As sea levels rise, Ms. Arnau foresaw East River Park evolving into eco-friendly marshes, managed by the Parks Department.
sentences.zh: 随着海平面上升，阿瑙预计东河公园将演变成由公园管理局管理的生态友好型沼泽地。

sentences.en: The group suggested that a truly enlightened response to climate change would be to build a green roof over the FDR Drive, an idea the big team had floated at the very start,
sentences.zh: 该组织建议，对气候变化真正开明的应对方式是在FDR大桥上方建造一个绿化屋顶，这是BIG团队在一开始就提出过的想法，

sentences.en: before city officials asked that it be withdrawn, because, as Amy Chester, the managing director of Rebuild, recalls,
sentences.zh: 在市官员要求撤回该想法之前，正如“重建”组织董事总经理艾米·切斯特所回忆的那样，

sentences.en: City Hall didn't want to, quote, overpromise.
sentences.zh: 当时市政厅不想“过度承诺”。

sentences.en: A roof, according to the East River Park Action Group, would create a protective barrier for the housing developments
sentences.zh: 东河公园行动组织认为，这样一个屋顶既能为住宅开发项目提供一道保护屏障，

sentences.en: while also muffling traffic noise and providing additional parkland.
sentences.zh: 同时还能消音降噪并提供额外的公园绿地。

sentences.en: In essence, they said, bury the highway, not the park.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，本质上应该是埋掉高速公路，而不是埋掉公园。

sentences.en: It's not a comprehensive plan, is how Ms. Cohen summed up criticism of the city's proposal.
sentences.zh: 科恩女士这样总结对市府提案的批评：这不是一个全面的计划。

sentences.en: It made no sense, the group argued, to cut down mature trees that provide shade, hold carbon, and act as a stopover for migratory birds, and replace them with saplings.
sentences.zh: 该组织辩称，砍掉那些提供阴凉、储存碳并作为候鸟中停站的成熟树木，并用树苗取而代之，这是毫无道理的。

sentences.en: Instead, they urged, focus on increasing the city's sewer capacity, upgrading public housing campuses, and reducing car emissions.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们敦促应专注于提高城市的下水道容量、升级公共住房园区以及减少汽车尾气排放。

sentences.en: I found it hard to argue in principle with their desires.
sentences.zh: 我发现从原则上很难反驳他们的诉求。

sentences.en: I also love the existing park, a shambolic retreat and slice of mid-century New York, which had some recent, costly upgrades, like a riverfront esplanade,
sentences.zh: 我也很喜欢现有的公园，这是一个凌乱而迷人的避难所，也是20世纪中期纽约的一片切片，这里最近刚进行了一些昂贵的升级，比如河滨长廊，

sentences.en: that will now need to be undone.
sentences.zh: 而这些现在都需要被拆除。

sentences.en: It's painful to imagine demolishing all those flower gardens,
sentences.zh: 想象一下拆除所有那些花圃、

sentences.en: WPA-era buildings, and playing fields.
sentences.zh: WPA时期的建筑和运动场，真是令人痛心。

sentences.en: New York's drainage and sewer systems are indeed rickety and ancient, a fact driven home in September, when a downpour from Tropical Storm Ida flooded city streets
sentences.zh: 纽约的排水和下水道系统确实破旧不堪、年代久远，9月份热带风暴“艾达”带来的暴雨淹没了城市街道，

sentences.en: and killed dozens of people in the region.
sentences.zh: 并导致该地区数十人死亡，这一事实更是给人们敲响了警钟。

sentences.en: But, constructing thousands of miles of new sewers, not to mention rerouting highways and other Herculean long-term measures, was never rebuilds, remit.
sentences.zh: 但是，建设数千英里的新下水道，更不用说重新规划高速公路和其他长期的艰巨措施，从来都不是“重建”组织的职责范围。

sentences.en: And at a certain point, making such lofty goals a prerequisite for urgently needed flood protection only ensures that nothing will get done.
sentences.zh: 而且在某种程度上，将这些崇高的目标作为获得迫切需要的防洪保护的前提条件，只会确保什么都做不成。

sentences.en: After meeting with Ms. Arnau and the other East River Park Action representatives, I visited Ms. Ortiz.
sentences.zh: 在与阿瑙女士和其他东河公园行动代表会面后，我去拜访了奥蒂斯女士。

sentences.en: She has become a frequently cited supporter of the city's plan.
sentences.zh: 她已经成为市府计划的一个经常被引用的支持者。

sentences.en: In January, after stepping down as Vladek's tenant president, she started working as a special assistant at the New York City Housing Authority, or NYCHA.
sentences.zh: 1月份，在卸任弗拉德克住户联合会主席后，她开始在纽约市住房管理局（简称NYCHA）担任特别助理。

sentences.en: We arranged a post-work late lunch at El Castillo de Agua Dos, a Dominican restaurant near the Vladek houses, where she kissed the waitress and waved to customers.
sentences.zh: 我们在弗拉德克公寓附近的一家名为El Castillo de Agua Dos的多米尼加餐厅安排了一顿工作后的迟午餐，在那里她亲吻了女服务员并向顾客挥手致意。

sentences.en: Frank Avila Goldman, a leader of the Residence Committee at Gouverneur Gardens, a development next to Vladek, joined us.
sentences.zh: 与弗拉德克毗邻的开发项目——总督花园（Gouverneur Gardens）的住宅委员会负责人弗兰克·阿维拉·戈德曼加入了我们。

sentences.en: Unlike Vladek, which sits on higher ground,
sentences.zh: 与地势较高的弗拉德克不同，

sentences.en: Gouverneur Gardens was badly flooded during Sandy.
sentences.zh: 总督花园在桑迪飓风期间遭到严重水淹。

sentences.en: When she first heard on the TV news that the city had discarded the original plan,
sentences.zh: 奥蒂斯女士说，当她第一次在电视新闻上听到市府废弃了最初的计划时，

sentences.en: Ms. Ortiz said, she was every bit as angry as Ms. Arnau and the other East River Park Action members.
sentences.zh: 她和阿瑙女士及其他东河公园行动成员一样愤怒。

sentences.en: The city scrambled to make up for its botched rollout by holding meetings with NYCHA.
sentences.zh: 市府通过与NYCHA举行会议，仓促弥补其笨拙的项目推出过程。

sentences.en: Carlina Rivera, a city council member representing the district, helped organize some of these meetings and noticed a gradual thaw among public housing residents.
sentences.zh: 代表该地区的市议会议员卡莉娜·里维拉帮助组织了其中一些会议，并注意到公房居民态度逐渐缓和。

sentences.en: They were upset by how the new plan had been announced,
sentences.zh: 里维拉女士说，

sentences.en: Ms. Rivera said, but at the end of the day, they wanted protection and wanted to know there would be a park for their grandchildren.
sentences.zh: 他们对新计划的公布方式感到不满，但归根结底，他们需要防洪保护，并希望确保他们的孙辈能有一个公园。

sentences.en: The obstacle to that aim, some of those NYCHA tenants came to believe, were now the members of East River Park Action and other such groups.
sentences.zh: 一些NYCHA租户开始认为，实现这一目标的障碍现在变成了东河公园行动和其他此类团体的成员。

sentences.en: Over the last several years, among the hundreds of thousands of residents in the area, a few thousand people signed petitions against the city's plan.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，该地区的数十万居民中，有几千人签署了反对市府计划的请愿书。

sentences.en: What percentage of the roughly 30,000 public housing residents objected to it isn't clear.
sentences.zh: 在大约3万名公房居民中，究竟有多少比例的人表示反对，目前尚不清楚。

sentences.en: But people like Ms. Ortiz and Mr. Avila Goldman began to zero in on how many of the most outspoken opponents seem to them to be white people not living in subsidized housing.
sentences.zh: 但像奥蒂斯女士和阿维拉·戈德曼先生这样的人开始注意到，许多声音最响亮的反对者似乎是不住在补贴住房中的白人。

sentences.en: For tenants in my building and the people I know in NYCHA who were slammed by Sandy, we need flood protection yesterday,
sentences.zh: 阿维拉·戈德曼先生告诉我：“对于我这栋楼的租户以及我在NYCHA认识的那些饱受桑迪飓风打击的人来说，我们需要昨天的防洪保护。”

sentences.en: Mr. Avila Goldman told me.
sentences.zh: “那些姗姗来迟的反对者却在谈论拯救树木和松鼠。”

sentences.en: The opponents who came late to the party talk about saving trees and squirrels.
sentences.zh: “我参加过太多这样的会议，感觉自己被居高临下地对待，仿佛只有白人才关心环境。”

sentences.en: I have been to so many meetings where I felt talked down to, as if only white people are the ones who care about the environment.
sentences.zh: “如果我有一根魔棒，”

sentences.en: If I had a magic wand,
sentences.zh: 如果我有一根魔杖，

sentences.en: I would also deck over the FDR drive, because when I open my windows, I find soot on my walls from all the traffic.
sentences.zh: 我还会把罗斯福大道上方盖起来，因为每当我打开窗户，车流带动的煤灰都会落满我的墙壁。

sentences.en: I'm on the front line.
sentences.zh: 我正身处前线。

sentences.en: But covering the highway is a pipe dream these people are using to derail a plan that is about saving our lives and our park.
sentences.zh: 但给高速公路加盖顶棚只是这些人用来破坏一项旨在拯救我们生命和公园的计划的白日梦。

sentences.en: As Ms. Ortiz put it, the new plan didn't blow up the community.
sentences.zh: 正如奥尔蒂斯女士所说，新计划并没有摧毁社区。

sentences.en: It revealed that there isn't a community.
sentences.zh: 它揭示出这里根本没有社区。

sentences.en: People like to throw around that word.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢随口抛出这个词。

sentences.en: It's not coincidental that the rise of community activism and the use of the word expertise occurred around the same time.
sentences.zh: 社区行动主义的兴起与专业知识一词的使用几乎发生在同一时期，这并非巧合。

sentences.en: Quote,
sentences.zh: 引述：

sentences.en: Expertise started to be commonly used only during the 1960s and 70s because there were suddenly conflicts over who should call themselves experts, says Gil Eyal,

sentences.en: Of course, the more expertise you have, the more entangled you probably are, meaning your neutrality is questionable,
sentences.zh: 当然，你拥有的专业知识越多，你所受到的牵连可能就越深，这意味着你的中立性令人怀疑，

sentences.en: Mr. Eyal said.
sentences.zh: 埃亚尔先生说。

sentences.en: So, the answer to that problem was to add yet more stakeholders, advocates, members of the public, which made consensus even harder to achieve.
sentences.zh: 因此，解决这个问题的办法是增加更多的利益相关者、倡导者和公众成员，这使得达成共识变得更加困难。

sentences.en: In essence,
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，

sentences.en: Mr. Eyal argues, a participatory system designed to build public trust causes people to lose faith in the system.
sentences.zh: 埃亚尔先生认为，一个旨在建立公众信任的参与式系统，反而导致人们对该系统失去信心。

sentences.en: The remedy, he says, is time.
sentences.zh: 他说，解决的办法是时间。

sentences.en: Researchers have a term, inclusion friction, he told me, for how bringing more voices into a process inevitably slows it down.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，研究人员有一个术语叫做“包容摩擦”，用来形容将更多声音引入一个过程是如何不可避免地将其拖慢的。

sentences.en: Conflicts arise among different stakeholders, and public discussions require explanations and careful conversations.
sentences.zh: 不同的利益相关者之间会产生冲突，公众讨论需要解释和深入的对话。

sentences.en: To do inclusion right, you have to take your time,
sentences.zh: 要把包容工作做好，你必须慢慢来，

sentences.en: Mr. Eyal says.
sentences.zh: 埃亚尔先生说。

sentences.en: You can't present people with a fait accompli because they'll understand the inclusion to have been a sham.
sentences.zh: 你不能向人们呈现既成事实，因为他们会认为这种包容是一场骗局。

sentences.en: The problem is that some crises don't afford the luxury of time.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，某些危机并没有给人留出充裕的时间。

sentences.en: A deadly virus racing around the world, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，一种在全球肆虐的致命病毒。

sentences.en: Operation Warp Speed, the federal COVID-19 vaccine development program, saved countless lives, but it also, quote, moved faster than public consensus, as Mr. Eyal points out,
sentences.zh: 正如埃亚尔先生所指出的，联邦新冠疫苗研发项目“极速行动”拯救了无数生命，但它也“超越了公众共识的发展速度”，

sentences.zh: 从而加剧了怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Some environmentalists argue that climate change is a crisis simply too big and fast-moving for the snail's pace of participatory democracy.
sentences.zh: 一些环保主义者认为，气候危机实在太大、发展太快，根本无法适应参与式民主那蜗牛般的速度。

sentences.en: The Dutch have resolved this conflict on the side of expertise.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人在这场冲突中站在了专业知识这一边。

sentences.en: With fully a third of the country below sea level, the Dutch have lived in a state of existential crisis for as long as they have occupied what is essentially the gutter of Europe,
sentences.zh: 由于全国足足有三分之一的土地低于海平面，自荷兰人占据这个基本上可以说是欧洲下水道的地方以来，他们就一直生活在生存危机之中，

sentences.en: where major rivers drain into the sea.
sentences.zh: 各大河流在这里汇入大海。

sentences.en: When he was tasked by President Obama with sandy recovery,
sentences.zh: 当奥巴马总统指派多诺万负责桑迪飓风过后的重建工作时，

sentences.en: During the 12th century, medieval Netherlanders established water boards, regional councils, in charge of overseeing canals, rivers, and everything else water-related.
sentences.zh: 在 12 世纪，中世纪的荷兰人就建立了水务委员会这一区域性议会，负责监督运河、河流以及所有与水相关的事物。

sentences.en: Today, Dutch water boards, in tandem with ecologists and engineers,
sentences.zh: 如今，荷兰水务委员会在生态学家和工程师的配合下，

sentences.en: still help determine national flood protection policies, including where people can or can't live and what needs to be built or unbuilt to safeguard against flooding.
sentences.zh: 依然在协助制定国家防洪政策，包括人们可以在哪里或不可以居住，以及需要建设或拆除哪些设施来防范洪水。

sentences.en: Elected politicians come and go.
sentences.zh: 当选的政治家来来去去。

sentences.en: Water boards are there to listen to science and take the long view.

sentences.en: In 1953, a huge winter storm in the North Sea breached dikes and flooded much of Western Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 1953 年，北海的一场巨大冬季风暴冲垮了堤防，淹没了荷兰西部的广大地区。

sentences.en: Nearly 2,000 people were killed.
sentences.zh: 近 2000 人丧生。

sentences.en: The Dutch still call it the disaster.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人至今仍将这场灾难称为“那场灾难”。

sentences.en: In response, officials undertook the Delta Works, a massive nationwide system of levees, sluices, dikes, dams, and seagates.
sentences.zh: 作为回应，官员们实施了“三角洲工程”，这是一套由堤坝、水闸、防洪堤、水坝和防潮闸组成的庞大全国性系统。

sentences.en: But even while the Delta Works were under construction, ecologists began to realize that some of those barriers were killing flora and fauna and disrupting tidal flows.
sentences.zh: 但就在三角洲工程建设期间，生态学家开始意识到，其中一些屏障正在杀死动植物并破坏潮汐流动。

sentences.en: So, simultaneously,
sentences.zh: 因此，与此同时，

sentences.en: Dutch water managers attempted a new approach.
sentences.zh: 荷兰水务管理者尝试了一种新方法。

sentences.en: Rather than just try to subjugate nature, they would also seed targeted areas to the rivers and sea.
sentences.zh: 他们不再仅仅试图征服自然，而是将部分指定区域重新交还给河流与大海。

sentences.en: At huge cost, the Dutch deconstructed some major daMs.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人不惜巨资拆除了一些主要水坝。

sentences.en: They built water parks that doubled as reservoirs and designed plazas with sunken gardens and basketball courts that collected runoff when nearby canals overflowed.
sentences.zh: 他们修建了兼作水库的水上公园，设计了带有下沉式花园和篮球场的广场，以便在附近运河满溢时收集径流。

sentences.en: They ordered farmers to move from properties that, based on engineers' calculations, would be needed as retention pools to prevent bigger cities downstream from flooding.
sentences.zh: 他们下令农民搬迁，因为根据工程师的计算，这些土地将被用作蓄水池，以防止下游的大城市被淹。

sentences.en: Farmers weren't happy.
sentences.zh: 农民们并不高兴。

sentences.en: But the lesson of the Delta Works was that progress is not an end point.
sentences.zh: 但三角洲工程给人们的教训是，进步不是一个终点。

sentences.en: It's a process.
sentences.zh: 而是一个过程。

sentences.en: In the Netherlands, citizens give up a measure of autonomy in return for safety.
sentences.zh: 在荷兰，公民为了换取安全而放弃了一定程度的自主权。

sentences.en: Prevention is the priority there.
sentences.zh: 预防在那里是重中之重。

sentences.en: In the United States, a different ethos reigns.
sentences.zh: 在美国，则奉行着一种不同的精神。

sentences.en: A nation steeped in individual liberty and manifest destiny is not accustomed to thinking about prevention or retreating from places too unsafe to occupy or too costly to save.
sentences.zh: 一个沉浸在个人自由与天定命运之中的国家，并不习惯去思考预防，也不习惯从那些过于危险而不宜居住或代价过于高昂而无法拯救的地方撤离。

sentences.en: This is New York, not New Amsterdam, as Mr. Ayal puts it.
sentences.zh: 正如阿亚尔先生所说，这里是纽约，而不是新阿姆斯特丹。

sentences.en: You can't impose a method here, he says, that is the result of, quote, collective learning handed down in big and small ways over centuries.
sentences.zh: 他说，你无法在这里强行推行一种方法，那是一种通过几个世纪以来大大小小的方式代代相传的“集体学习”的结果。

sentences.en: What we can learn from the Dutch, he suggests, is that some of our truisms are not as stable as we think.
sentences.zh: 他建议，我们能从荷兰人身上学到的是，我们的一些陈词滥调并没有想象中那么稳固。

sentences.en: Participation and transparency are not an absolute good.
sentences.zh: 参与和透明度并非绝对的美德。

sentences.zh: 我的首要任务永远是给那些没有声音的人发声。

sentences.en: Mr. Arouse, the New York University graduate student, told me he believes finding common ground has to start long before a crisis arises.
sentences.zh: 纽约大学的研究生阿鲁斯先生告诉我，他相信寻找共识必须在危机爆发前很久就开始。

sentences.zh: 穿过一座横跨高速公路的老旧人行天桥，我们来到了公园，路过了一个带有混凝土国际象棋桌的老旧游乐场，奥尔蒂斯女士曾告诉我，她以前经常带孩子们来这里
